_about: Synthetic podcast transcript for the highlights evaluation. Lines 6-13 are a self-contained story (about 62s); lines 18-25 are release-timing advice (about 57s). The rest is small talk, admin and an outro.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Okay, we're recording. Welcome back to Loose Ends.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: I'm here with Maya Okafor, who just finished her first headline tour.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Hi, thanks for having me. Sorry I was late, the traffic was awful.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: No worries. Did you get a coffee? There's some in the kitchen.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I'm fine, I've had three already today.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Fair enough. So, before the tour, I want to go back to the very beginning.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Tell me about your first ever gig, because I've heard it did not go to plan.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Oh no. Okay. So I'm nineteen, I've booked a slot at a pub in Leeds, and I've told everyone I know.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I walk on stage, I plug in my guitar, and the whole pub's power goes out. Every light, the fridges, everything.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: No way. What did you do?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The landlord's shouting, people are using their phone torches, and I just thought, well, I'm here now.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: So I unplugged, stood on a chair in the middle of the room and played the whole set acoustic in the dark.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: And honestly it's still the best gig I've ever played. Forty people singing along by torchlight. I've been chasing that feeling ever since.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: That's incredible. That's a film scene.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Quick note for listeners: this episode is out on Thursday, and the video is on our channel.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: If you want to support the show there's a link in the description.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Do you want me to mention the merch?

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Go for it. Anyway. Let's talk about the new single.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: A lot of artists listening want to know how you plan a release. What's your approach?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The biggest mistake I made early on was announcing a song the same week it came out. Nobody had time to care.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Now I start eight weeks out. I tease a fifteen second clip, I let people ask what it is, and I don't answer yet.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Four weeks out I open the pre-save and show the cover. Two weeks out I play it live and film the crowd.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: By release day, people feel like they've been part of it. That's the whole trick, make them feel involved before it exists.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: So it's less about the song and more about the story around it.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: The song has to be good. But a good song nobody's waiting for just disappears.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: That's such useful advice.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Okay, we're nearly out of time. Where can people find you?

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: I'm Maya Okafor everywhere. The single's out on the twentieth.

segments.speaker: Speaker 1
segments.text: Amazing. Thanks for coming in.

segments.speaker: Speaker 2
segments.text: Thanks for having me.
